_: Text of the README 'How it works' figure (v2/where-chock-sits.png), read by where-chock-sits.mjs. Component names are generic: no vendor is named. 'points' is every place Chock meets the agent or the repository, in session order: 'label' is drawn on the marker, 'kind' is its style (all = solid: every agent; hooks = outlined: only where the agent has hooks or a gateway), 'name', 'line' and 'scope' are the list in docs/architecture.md. tests/test_readme_picture.py derives the same list from the engine (Surface enum, git script events, the agentseam events chock uses) and fails when they differ. 'proof' lists the tests that prove each point (checked, not drawn). Not drawn, because the engine does not wire them: a prompt-submit hook; the managed-setting and gateway surfaces.
title: You keep working with your agent as before. Chock checks each action before it lands.

chock.name: Chock
chock.line: a local program; its rules are files in your repository; no model, no tokens

footer: The rules are files in your repository. A person turns them on once with chock sync.
alt: A layered sketch: you ask a coding agent for a change, and inside the agent a model and an agent loop work with context and call tools, some through an MCP server. Chock sits below with a marker on each place it meets them: session start, rules in context, before and after each tool, the end of the turn and the MCP gateway, then commit, push and CI in your repository; solid markers apply to every agent, outlined ones only where the agent has hooks.

points.name: Session start
points.line: arms the hooks from what is committed.
points.label: session start

points.name: Rules in context
points.line: a short rules block Chock writes into AGENTS.md. Advisory.
points.label: rules

points.name: Before a tool runs
points.line: Chock judges the call: allow, ask or block. A refusal goes back to the model with one line on what to do instead.
points.label: pre-tool

points.name: After a tool runs
points.line: records what ran, for checks that read the session. It never changes a verdict.
points.label: post-tool

points.name: End of the turn
points.line: reads what the turn left in the working tree and refuses to end the turn on a finding. A backstop.
points.label: stop

points.name: MCP gateway
points.line: a proxy that judges calls to an MCP server.
points.scope: where a server is set up through it
points.label: MCP gateway

points.name: In CI
points.line: the same gates on the pull request.
points.label: CI
